text:
maria: heads-up — canary rollout of r/3421 (quant-int8-dispatch) is showing a ~12% increase in p95 token latency on prod-nyc. holding the rollout. commit: aa7c9d2
ops-bot: [perf-alert] canary p95 delta +12% vs baseline for /v1/generate (model: redwood-int8-1). CI perf check failed: https://ci.internal/runs/9876 :alarm_clock:
tyler: any initial traces or flamegraphs?
maria: attaching quick profile from a canary box (5m sampling) — big callouts below:
```
pprof top -cum
Showing nodes accounting for 62.3s, 100% of 62.3s total\      flat  flat%   sum%        cum   cum%   name
     8.1s 13.0% 13.0%    35.8s 57.5%  dequant::apply
     6.0s 9.6% 22.6%    22.1s 35.5%  kernel_selector::choose_kernel
     5.5s 8.8% 31.4%    28.3s 45.4%  kv_cache::evict_if_needed
     4.0s 6.4% 37.8%    10.0s 16.1%  packer::pack_tokens
```
The cum numbers look like dequant and kernel selection are dominating. Also seeing lots of small allocations in the flamegraph around kv cache paths.
jonathan: that kv_cache::evict_if_needed spike is suspicious — could be a regression in the quant-hotpath that increases transient memory use and triggers evictions more often. evictions + re-populate = copy storms and extra dequant calls. do we have kv occupancy telemetry?
maria: yes — from the same canary window: median kv_entries per request increased from 48 -> 72 and eviction rate went up x3. Telemetry link: https://telemetry.internal/kv/1601
kim: ran a controlled microbench on a dev rig reproducing canary profile. Before (mainline pre-r/3421): p95=72ms, after: p95=81ms. I measured avg allocator churn +30% and observed an extra memcpy per token in the trace. Minimal repro steps below:
```
# repro script
python perf_repro.py --model redwood-int8-1 --seq 1024 --batch 1 --requests 2000
# results saved to out/bench.json
```
kim: attaching small stack from perf:
```
#0 dequant::apply
#1 kernel_selector::dequant_then_kernel
#2 kv_cache::read_or_fill
#3 runtime::serve_request
```
bench-bot: CI perf job failed on mainline post-merge for r/3421: https://ci.internal/job/quant-perf/515 (regression threshold +8% on p95) :x:
sara: can we bisect the merge set? r/3421 itself touches kernel selector heuristics and adds a fallback path that triggers a dequant path on mixed-precision models. suspect change: selector now prefers smaller kernels at medium sequence lengths which forces dequant+copy.
tyler: I'll bisect between aa7c9d2 (post-merge) and parent 8f1b2a0. plan: do 4-run binary search on canary harness, verify p95 and eviction rate. starting now.
maria: re: rollback policy — if bisect reproduces and it's the selector change, we should revert that piece immediately (it was a behavior change, not critical correctness). please coordinate w/ releases.
tyler: quick note — I found a short-term mitigation: disable the new 'micropref' heuristic via env var QUANT_SELECTOR_MICROPREF=0 — toggling that on the canary restores p95 to 73ms and eviction rate back to baseline. opening revert/shim PR.
jonathan: good find. that suggests a kernel size mismatch causing larger KV working set. we should also add an integration test covering kv occupancy for selector changes.
maria: can someone open the revert and add the test? ops will hold the full rollout until revert lands and passes canary.
tyler: opening revert PR now: https://git.internal/r/3499 (revert: disable micropref heuristic). will attach bench runs.
kim: +1 on adding kv occupancy test, I'm happy to draft the test (small harness that asserts eviction rate delta < 1.2x under standard load).
sara: assigning follow-ups: tyler -> revert PR + canary runs, kim -> kv-occupancy test draft, jonathan -> postmortem notes (root cause analysis). maria -> communicate to releases and mark rollout hold.
maria: thanks. I'll post an announcement to #incidents and tag release leads. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: deploy-hold set for rollout r/3421 by maria at 1797654328
